- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from bullish to bearish, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and scale down gradually.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth 3–5 day moving average of forecast to reduce noise and align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows mean reversion, forecast should be anchored to 10–15 day moving average of past 30 days.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes or reversal is confirmed.
